requirements.fix: Fix the agent user first (see the scan finding), then make sure the user exists in the target org.
requirements.message: CustomerServiceAgent runs as an agent user, which is a Salesforce user record, not metadata. It does not travel with the story and must already exist in Passport-QA. The agent file does not name a user that will exist there.

proposedStep.instructions:
Before deploying, in the Passport-QA org:
1. Create the agent user if it does not exist: sf org create agent-user --target-org <Passport-QA alias>
2. Assign the permission sets the agent's actions need to that user (sf org assign permset --on-behalf-of <agent username>).
3. Make sure the agent file or sfdx-project.json "replacements" give this environment's agent username.
proposedStep.name: Agent user for CustomerServiceAgent exists in Passport-QA

requirements.fix: Add a post-deployment step to the user story that publishes and activates the agent, or keep the agent's GenAiPlannerBundle in source control so deployment publishes it.
requirements.message: Deploying the authoring bundle does not make CustomerServiceAgent live. Without its GenAiPlannerBundle in source control, the agent must be published and activated in Passport-QA after every deployment.

proposedStep.instructions:
After deploying, in the Passport-QA org:
sf agent publish authoring-bundle --api-name CustomerServiceAgent --target-org <Passport-QA alias>
sf agent activate --api-name CustomerServiceAgent --target-org <Passport-QA alias>
proposedStep.name: Publish and activate CustomerServiceAgent in Passport-QA

findings.message: Flow "EscalateCase" will not arrive in Passport-QA: it only exists as an uncommitted local file; commit it to the story so the promotion carries it.
